note: Recorded off a running prismd by crates/prismd/tests/ui_show.rs. The sequences, the presets, the executors and every answer are the daemon's own, taken from a fresh client's snapshot. Regenerate with: cargo test -p prismd --test ui_show -- --ignored

steps.what: make a cue list to store into: a fresh show has none at all
put it on an executor, which is what makes it playable
and put it in force, which is what a store with no cue list named goes into — S39's session field, and the decision S28 marked
select three PARs
and dial them red
what would storing cue 1 do? it does not exist yet, so this is a create
store it
select two of them again
and dial them green
what would storing cue 1 again do? **this is the overwrite an operator has to be told about**: the three reds are still in the programmer, so they are replaced, and the two greens are added

and the same store as an Override? the same two added and the same three replaced, and **nothing thrown away** — because this programmer happens to hold everything the cue holds, which is the case where the two modes coincide and an operator needs to be able to see that they do
and as a Remove? it writes nothing at all: the three values the cue and the programmer share are what goes
store it as a Merge, which is what the operator chose
store a second cue
name it
give it a fade
and a trigger that carries a time with it
renumber it to 1.5, which moves it up the list
a fade that runs backwards: refused, and nothing moves
a renumber onto a number that is taken: refused, and nothing moves
clear the programmer
select the PARs again
dial a blue
and a dimmer value on a PAR's white
what would storing preset 1 in the Colour pool do? a create, and it counts the colour values only
store it, with a name and a scribble-strip colour
clear again
select the PARs
and apply the preset, which is what puts a **link** in the programmer
store a cue out of it: its parts carry the preset reference
clear once more
select the PARs
dial a different blue
what would storing over preset 1 do? an edit of a preset: the three blues are replaced and the three whites are kept
edit the preset — **and cue 3 follows it**, which is the whole claim
a preview of a store into a sequence that is not there: refused, in the daemon's own words
clear the programmer for the last time
and a preview with nothing to store: refused, but it still says what is filed under that number
load cue 3 back into the programmer — **its preset links come with it**, which is the claim `EditCue` exists to keep
put it straight back with nothing changed: **byte-identical**, links and all, and the Update key stops blinking
now change something while the cue is loaded, which is what makes the key blink
and put that back
an Update after the programmer has been cleared: refused, because clearing the programmer clears the update state
...and this is the refusal
select a PAR
dial a green on it
what would an Override of cue 1 do now? **this is the one an operator has to be warned about**: one value replaced and four thrown away
store it as an Override: the cue ends up holding exactly this one value, and the four that were there are gone
and a Remove of the same value from cue 1.5, which holds four others: one goes and four stay
take it out with a **Remove**: the cue keeps everything else
the same Remove again: refused, because the value is gone and a store that removes nothing is one an operator would press twice
append the programmer to the cue list: a new cue at the highest number, which is 4
and merge it into every cue there is
delete a cue: the numbers left do not close up
delete a cue that is not there: refused, and nothing moves
a sequence number that is taken: refused, and the cue list survives
fire the list
step it again
and stop it
a Go on an executor with nothing on it: refused
and take the last edit back
